info.name: Zameens — Organizations & Members
info.description:
Every organization- and member-lifecycle endpoint in one place — both self-service (organizations.routes.js, run as the org owner or an invited member) and admin-only (organizations.admin.routes.js, run as an ADMIN-role user). Responses use the standard { success, data, meta } / { success, error } envelope.

Suggested run order: Auth — Org Owner (Request OTP → set {{otp}} from the server console → Verify OTP) → Organizations / Create organization → Members / Add member (invite by phone) (creates the unverified account for {{memberPhone}}) → Auth — Member User (logs into that same account via SMS OTP, proving it) → Members / Accept membership (as member user) → Auth — Admin (see that folder's Request OTP description — needs the ADMIN role granted directly in the DB first, no self-service path exists) → Admin — Organizations / Admin — Members as needed.

Verified end-to-end against a real local instance (all 4 self-service org endpoints, 4 member endpoints, 5 admin org endpoints, 1 admin member endpoint, plus the invalid-transition, last-owner, and PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED guards). One inconsistency found along the way, not fixed here: requireAdmin (admin routes) returns 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED for both a missing token and a valid-but-non-admin token, where requireAuth (self-service routes) correctly returns 401 for a missing token — a client can't tell "log in" from "forbidden" on admin routes.

Plan & usage pooling (why PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED behaves the way it does above): the org's plan lives on one commerce.plan_subscriptions row keyed by organizationId, and every usage counter that reads it (active listings, AI monthly quota, featured-listing/other subscription-usage ledger entries, team-member seats) filters purely on organization_id — never on which member did the thing. OWNER, ADMIN, and MEMBER all draw from and count against the exact same shared pool with zero role distinction; the org-membership check gating who can attribute a resource to the org (used throughout this collection) is likewise role-blind — only status = 'ACTIVE' is checked. The one caveat: this pooling is never inferred from "the actor happens to be a member of some org" — it only kicks in when the client explicitly passes organizationId on the resource-creation call (listing, property, AI conversation — all outside this collection's scope). A member acting without it draws against their own personal plan instead, silently.

variable.description: Org owner's bearer token — set by Auth — Org Owner / Verify OTP.
The phone number Members / Add member (invite by phone) invites, and Auth — Member User later logs into — keep these in sync if you change it.
Invited user's bearer token — set by Auth — Member User / Verify OTP (run Add member (invite by phone) first).
Invited user's own id — auto-captured on Auth — Member User / Verify OTP, or read it off Add member (invite by phone)'s response. Used by Remove member and Admin — Members / Update member status.
Bearer token for a user with the ADMIN role — set by Auth — Admin / Verify OTP.
Shared scratch variable — set by whichever Request OTP call you just ran.
OTP code from the delivery provider (logged to console in non-production). Shared across all three Auth folders — log in one identity at a time.

item.name: Verify OTP
item.description: OTP is logged to the server console in non-production — set the {{otp}} collection variable from there before running this.

item.name: Request OTP
item.description: Run Members / Add member (invite by phone) first — this logs in as the account that invite just created (or reused) for {{memberPhone}}.

item.name: Verify OTP
item.description: OTP is logged to the server console in non-production — set the {{otp}} collection variable from there before running this.

item.name: Request OTP
item.description: No self-service path grants ADMIN. Before this will work, the destination phone must already have the role: INSERT INTO auth.user_roles (user_id, role_id) SELECT '<user id>', id FROM auth.roles WHERE code = 'ADMIN'. If the account already exists and is logged in elsewhere, Auth — Admin / Refresh token alone (not a full re-verify) is enough to pick up a role granted after the fact.

item.name: Verify OTP
item.description: OTP is logged to the server console in non-production — set the {{otp}} collection variable from there before running this.

item.name: Create organization
item.description: The creator is auto-added as OWNER, and the org is also granted a real, admin-editable Free plan row (same as an individual gets on registration).

item.name: My organizations
item.description: Scoped to the caller's own memberships only — for a platform-wide listing (any org, any status), see Admin — Organizations / List organizations. Filters: search, name, type, slug, phone, email, gstNumber, reraNumber, status, role.

item.name: Organization details
item.description: Public/optional-auth — works with or without a bearer token. 404s a PENDING or SUSPENDED organization unless the caller is one of its active members (admins are not exempt — see Admin — Organizations / Organization detail for the admin-safe equivalent).

item.name: Update organization
item.description: Requires the caller to be an active OWNER or ADMIN of the org. Only send the fields you want to change.

item.name: List members
item.description: Requires the caller to already be an active member of the org (any role) — this is what 403s a non-member admin, see Admin — Organizations / Organization detail for the workaround.

item.name: Add member (invite by phone)
item.description: Invite-by-phone only — there is no explicit-userId variant. Requires the caller to be an active OWNER or ADMIN of the org. If {{memberPhone}} already belongs to an existing user, that account is added as-is (name untouched) — otherwise a new, unverified account is created (phone_verified_at stays null until proven via Auth — Member User below). Grants no platform role. role only accepts ADMIN or MEMBER — there is no way to grant OWNER here. Adding a genuinely new member is checked against the org's plan team-member limit — returns 403 PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED once at the plan's teamMembers cap (ACTIVE + INVITED both count). A brand-new org's FREE plan defaults to teamMembers: 1 (DEFAULT_FREE_TEAM_MEMBERS), and the OWNER already occupies that one seat — so this very first invite can 403 immediately on a fresh org. Confirmed live: this needs a real commerce.plan_subscriptions row for the org with a higher teamMembers to get past it (see the Zameens — Commerce & Payments collection's Admin — plan catalog / checkout flow for the real purchase path — there's no dev seed script for this yet). Run this BEFORE Auth — Member User.

item.name: Accept membership (as member user)
item.description: Run as the invited user, not the org owner — uses {{memberAccessToken}} (from Auth — Member User), not the collection default {{accessToken}}. The only path that moves a membership from INVITED to ACTIVE.

item.name: Remove member
item.description: Requires the caller to be an active OWNER or ADMIN of the org (and OWNER specifically to remove another OWNER). Blocks with 400 LAST_OWNER if the target is the org's only active owner. For an admin override that bypasses the OWNER/ADMIN requirement (and can also reactivate a REMOVED member), see Admin — Members / Update member status.

item.name: List organizations
item.description: Platform-wide, not scoped to the caller's own memberships (unlike My organizations above) — PENDING and SUSPENDED organizations are visible here too. Filters: search, name, type, slug, phone, email, gstNumber, reraNumber, status.

item.name: Organization detail
item.description: Same as Organization details above but bypasses its active-membership visibility gate, so a PENDING or SUSPENDED organization can be reviewed before/without approving it. Also inlines a members array (user/role/status/joinedAt per member) — the public detail response never includes this, and List members above would 403 an admin who isn't themselves a member.

item.name: Approve organization
item.description: PENDING → ACTIVE. 409 INVALID_TRANSITION if not currently PENDING.

item.name: Suspend organization
item.description: PENDING or ACTIVE → SUSPENDED (doubles as rejecting a pending org — there's no separate REJECTED status in this schema). reason is required. 409 INVALID_TRANSITION if already SUSPENDED.

item.name: Reinstate organization
item.description: SUSPENDED → ACTIVE. 409 INVALID_TRANSITION if not currently SUSPENDED.

item.name: Update member status
item.description: Sets a member's status directly to ACTIVE, INVITED, or REMOVED, bypassing the org's own OWNER/ADMIN requirement entirely (unlike Remove member above). Unlike Remove member, this can also reactivate a REMOVED member straight to ACTIVE/INVITED with no fresh invite-accept cycle and no team-member seat-limit re-check — a deliberate admin override. Still blocks 400 LAST_OWNER if the target is the org's only active OWNER and the new status isn't ACTIVE. There's no SUSPENDED member status distinct from REMOVED without a schema migration.
